c3_5_marsh_of_soldiers.complete: Good... These helmets will be recorded only as «Aesir soldiers betrayed». No need to ask why every helmet faces toward the spring. I will keep them myself.

c3_6_withering.title: Withered from Within
c3_6_withering.desc: The Withered Grove is full of trees dead from the inside. Cut down the ones still walking, then examine the dried-up stream.
c3_6_withering.offer: Trees in the Withered Grove have risen and started walking, though they're dead inside... Cut down the rampaging ones, then go see the stream in the middle of the grove with your own eyes — see «which way» the water went.
c3_6_withering.progress: 10 withered treants, then examine the stream in the middle of the Withered Grove.
c3_6_withering.complete: Every root points north... toward the great tree. That's where this world's life has been pulled, ever since the day the army marched through the gate.

c3_7_sentinels_still_standing.title: The Sentinels Still Standing
c3_7_sentinels_still_standing.desc: The stone sentinels of the Withered Grove have gone mad. Collect sentinel cores so Galla can repair armor.
c3_7_sentinels_still_standing.offer: The Vanir sentinels... my ancestors built them to guard the spring. Not against monsters — against «gods». Now their cores have decayed and they've all gone mad. Bring me three cores and I'll make you armor.
c3_7_sentinels_still_standing.progress: 8 Vanir sentinels and 3 sentinel cores, in the Withered Grove.
c3_7_sentinels_still_standing.complete: The core still glows green... three hundred years and it still does its duty. Here's armor made from its stone plates. Wear it, and remember who it was built to stand against.

c3_8_stake_burned_thrice.title: The Stake Burned Thrice
c3_8_stake_burned_thrice.desc: Eskil sends you to clear the warrior spirits of the Forgotten Battlefield and examine the burnt stake and old banner for the chronicle.
c3_8_stake_burned_thrice.offer: Aesir soldiers' spirits still linger on the old battlefield. Destroy them so they may rest... and meanwhile, look at the burnt stake and the buried banner, then come back and tell me what you saw. I shall «record it correctly».
c3_8_stake_burned_thrice.progress: 12 Aesir warrior spirits, then examine the burnt stake and the buried banner on the Forgotten Battlefield.
c3_8_stake_burned_thrice.complete: You've seen the stake... Gullveig, the witch who incited the war, burned three times for her crimes — that is the version the Temple records. Now tell me, which way would you have me write it?
c3_8_stake_burned_thrice.choice: Eskil opens the chronicle, pen hovering over the page — «Vanaheim, the year of the war... which side began it?»
opts: Record that the Vanir started it (per the Temple)
Record what I saw — the Aesir marched in

c3_9_thorn_matriarch.title: The Thorn Matriarch
c3_9_thorn_matriarch.desc: The Thorn Matriarch blocks the way to the Spring of Life. Bring her down to open the path.
c3_9_thorn_matriarch.offer: The way to the spring is sealed by a thicket of thorns, and the Thorn Matriarch is inside... She protected the spring before there were any gods at all, but now she can't tell friend from foe. You have to bring her down. I'm sorry.
c3_9_thorn_matriarch.progress: The Thorn Matriarch is at the far east of the Forgotten Battlefield. Watch for thorns bursting up from the ground — when the ground cracks, dash away at once.
c3_9_thorn_matriarch.complete: ...She has fallen. I can hear the thorns withdrawing from this place. Take this shield, woven from her thorns, so she can go on protecting you.

c3_10_flame_that_never_dies.title: The Flame That Never Dies
c3_10_flame_that_never_dies.desc: Put out Gullveig's Flame in the Spring of Life, then see what's hidden at the bottom of the spring.
c3_10_flame_that_never_dies.offer: In the middle of the spring burns a flame that has burned for three hundred years... Gullveig, who refused to give up the spring, was burned three times, and three times she rose again. Now she is nothing but flame. Put her out, and see what they hid beneath that flame.
c3_10_flame_that_never_dies.progress: Gullveig's Flame is in the middle of the Spring of Life, east past the Forgotten Battlefield — she unleashes three waves of fire. Watch the timing and dash away.
c3_10_flame_that_never_dies.complete: The «Drain» rune... the same one the dwarves saw on the hammerhead. Here it doesn't drain iron, child. It drains the life of the whole world and sends it north... for three hundred years now.
c3_10_flame_that_never_dies.choice: Njorda: «You've seen who is drawing the life from this world... Will you tell the people of Midgard?»
opts: I'll tell everyone
...Not yet. No one would believe it.
c3_10_flame_that_never_dies.cutscene:
The song you used to hear every day has fallen silent.

Frida stands at the gate, looking north.

...the way every root points.

c4_1_gate_of_giants.title: A Gate Too Tall to Reach
c4_1_gate_of_giants.desc: Meet the people of Utgard — the guard, the merchant, and the priest who followed you from the Temple.
c4_1_gate_of_giants.offer:
A human walked through the pass alone, with no army behind... So you didn't come here to kill anyone.

Before you walk my city, let the people know your face. Thjazi at the gate, Hymir at the market, and the priest from your Temple who followed you here — he's been waiting outside my house since morning.
c4_1_gate_of_giants.progress: Thjazi will curse at you — let him. Hymir will try to sell you things. As for Asmund... listen to him carefully. Not everything he says is wrong.
c4_1_gate_of_giants.complete:
That's everyone... Here — the Jotun Seal. Carry it, and the people of this city will know you're a guest, not an enemy.

The last human who received this seal... what was his name? Strange. I can't remember. As if someone erased that name from my head.

c4_2_wolves_at_the_pass.title: Wolves at the Pass
c4_2_wolves_at_the_pass.desc: Frost wolves and snow hawks are ambushing caravans in the Frost Pass. Deal with them.
c4_2_wolves_at_the_pass.offer:
My caravan hasn't made it into the city in three weeks. The frost wolves hunt in packs, and the snow hawks swoop from above.

Thin their numbers a little. I'll pay in goods — the finest wolf-fur coat in my shop.
c4_2_wolves_at_the_pass.progress: 20 frost wolves and 12 snow hawks, in the Frost Pass — the way you came in.
c4_2_wolves_at_the_pass.complete:
The road's much clearer... Here's the wolf-fur coat. I've cut it to fit you.

Know why the wolves came down as far as the pass? There's something up north they're afraid of.

c4_3_what_the_temple_teaches.title: What the Temple Teaches
c4_3_what_the_temple_teaches.desc: Hunt 15 ice trolls on the Giant Steppe, then bring the Temple primer to Elder Skadi.
c4_3_what_the_temple_teaches.offer:
I brought the primer the Temple uses to teach children. The first chapter says: «Giants are the enemies of mankind.»

The ice trolls on the steppe are always attacking travelers. Deal with them first — let me see that the giants' land does have real beasts. Then take this primer to Elder Skadi. I want to know what she'll say.
c4_3_what_the_temple_teaches.progress: 15 ice trolls on the Giant Steppe, then take the primer to Skadi.
c4_3_what_the_temple_teaches.complete:
What did she say... She laughed, didn't she?

I'm not angry. It's just... that primer taught me my whole life. If half of it is wrong, what about the other half? Is that wrong too?
c4_3_what_the_temple_teaches.choice: Skadi asks you to read the primer aloud in the middle of the city — including the line «Giants eat children», in front of the giant children.
opts: Read it aloud (Skadi laughs, Thjazi is furious)
Keep the primer, don't read it

c4_4_child_who_asks.title: The Child Who Asks
c4_4_child_who_asks.desc: Talk to Leif the giant child, then walk through the mammoth herd on the Giant Steppe to the end without killing a single mammoth.
c4_4_child_who_asks.offer:
Leif, my grandson, goes around asking everyone whether humans really eat children. Go answer him, won't you.

Then go to the Giant Steppe and walk through the mammoth herd to the far end — don't draw your sword on them. Mammoths harm no one who doesn't harm them first.
c4_4_child_who_asks.progress: Leif is at the edge of town near the graveyard. On the steppe, walk to the herd's crossing at the far end. Kill no mammoth from the moment you enter — if you slip up, leave the steppe and come back in.
c4_4_child_who_asks.complete:
You walked through the herd and not one of them died... Leif was watching the whole time.

He knitted you a scarf. It's a bit big for a human, but wear it. When you reach Alfheim, it will mean more than you think.

c4_5_wall_they_call_ours.title: The Wall They Call Theirs
c4_5_wall_they_call_ours.desc: Hunt 12 giant stone soldiers at the Broken Wall, then read the giant inscription on the wall.
c4_5_wall_they_call_ours.offer:
Back home you call the southern wall «the Wall Against Giants», don't you? The Temple teaches that humans built it to keep us out.

Go see for yourself. The stone soldiers there still patrol by orders given three hundred years ago. Deal with them, then read the inscription on the wall — in the giants' tongue, the side no human ever reads.
c4_5_wall_they_call_ours.progress: 12 giant stone soldiers, then find the giant inscription on the wall. The letters are as big as a door — you can't miss them.
c4_5_wall_they_call_ours.complete:
«Built to hold back the danger from the sky, not to hold back people» — that's what the inscription says. My ancestors built that wall, not humans.

And the «danger from the sky»... means the ones who came down with the lightning. Take this shield. It was cut from the same stone as the wall.

c4_6_fourth_rune.title: The Fourth Rune
c4_6_fourth_rune.desc: Bring Gerd giant stone cores and frost fangs so she can carve a rune.
c4_6_fourth_rune.offer: I'll carve a rune for you to see — but I need good stone. Five stone cores from the chests of giant stone soldiers, and ten frost wolf fangs to make the chisel.
c4_6_fourth_rune.progress: 5 giant stone cores, from stone soldiers in the Frozen Hall or at the wall · 10 frost fangs, from frost wolves.
c4_6_fourth_rune.complete:
The fourth, «Genesis»... Do you hear the chisel? It cries just like the day Thor took it from us.

Take this carving hammer. I don't need it anymore. One day you'll have to carve something that even I can't.

c4_7_hall_of_ice.title: The Hall the Ice Remembers
c4_7_hall_of_ice.desc: Hunt 15 echo wraiths in the Frozen Hall, then look at the ancient painting on the wall.
c4_7_hall_of_ice.offer:
The giants say there's a painting in the Frozen Hall that «proves everything». I want to see it with my own eyes... and I want you to see it too.

But the hall is full of the spirits of soldiers from both sides. Deal with them first, then look at the painting.
c4_7_hall_of_ice.progress: 15 echo wraiths, then look at the painting in the middle of the hall. I'll wait here... I don't dare go look myself yet.
c4_7_hall_of_ice.complete:
...You've seen it. I've seen it too — I followed you in.

The army in the painting storms into the city. It came to protect no one. And the man with the hammer leads the way.

This is Chronicle Volume VII — the volume the Temple says «never existed». I could only tear out half. Keep it with you.
c4_7_hall_of_ice.choice:
Asmund: «A painting... can lie. Giants who paint it themselves would paint themselves in the right.»
What do you say?
opts: «You've seen it and you still say that?»
«The painting might really lie. We need other proof.»

c4_8_shieldbearer.title: The One Still Standing Watch
c4_8_shieldbearer.desc: Bring down the Shieldbearer of the Wall, who still blocks the way to the Lightning Heart Crater.
c4_8_shieldbearer.offer:
The Shieldbearer... the last giant soldier still standing guard on the wall. He's stood there three hundred years, until he no longer remembers what he's guarding.

He lets no one pass to the Lightning Heart Crater, giant or human. I don't want to ask you to kill him... but if you're to reach the crater, there's no other way.
c4_8_shieldbearer.progress: The Shieldbearer is at the tower on the eastern end of the wall. Beware when he slams his shield — the shockwave runs out both left and right.
c4_8_shieldbearer.complete:
Did he say anything before he died... «I stood on the wrong side», didn't he?

This is his armor, the last giant of the wall — wear it, and let it keep standing watch on you.

Don't go to the crater tonight. At night on the wall... there's something the living shouldn't see. But you may have to.

c4_9_breach_on_the_south.title: The Breach Is on the South
c4_9_breach_on_the_south.desc: Examine the breach in the wall, then speak with Asmund again.
c4_9_breach_on_the_south.offer:
The Shieldbearer has fallen and the way to the crater is open... but before you go, I want you to look at the breach in the wall once more, carefully.

See which way the rubble flew, then tell Asmund, your priest, what you saw.
c4_9_breach_on_the_south.progress: The breach is in the middle of the Broken Wall. Study its edges, then go talk to Asmund.
c4_9_breach_on_the_south.complete:
The rubble lies on our side... which means the wall was smashed in from the south — the human side.

Asmund says he'll go back and ask the Temple, doesn't he... He's a good man, human. I hope the Temple won't punish him just for asking.

c4_10_heart_of_lightning.title: The Heart Still Beating
c4_10_heart_of_lightning.desc: Bring down Stone Hrungnir in the Lightning Heart Crater, then examine what lies in its chest.
c4_10_heart_of_lightning.offer:
Hrungnir, marshal of the giants, fought Thor one-on-one and died — that's where your legend ends.

But the next night, his corpse rose, and destroyed the city he once protected with his own hands.

Go to the Lightning Heart Crater and bring him down... then see what's buried in his chest.
c4_10_heart_of_lightning.progress: Stone Hrungnir is at the bottom of the crater, east of the wall. Near the end of the fight, its chest will open — that's your moment.
c4_10_heart_of_lightning.complete:
A lightning heart... carved with the hammer emblem. Thor didn't destroy our city himself. He planted this heart so our own marshal would rise and destroy his own city.

Leif has been watching from afar since you went into the crater. He's not afraid of you anymore.

Go. Alfheim is to the north, where the root breaks out of the crater. Mind the light.
c4_10_heart_of_lightning.choice: The lightning heart still thumps in your hand... What will you do with it?
opts: Smash it — let Hrungnir finally rest (evidence lost)
Keep it as evidence (receive «Lightning Heart»)
c4_10_heart_of_lightning.cutscene: Leif stands at the crater's edge, so far away he looks tiny... He waves to you, then runs back to the city.

c5_1_city_without_night.title: The City Without Night
c5_1_city_without_night.desc: Meet the people of Ljosalf, and ask each of them «What about the night?»
c5_1_city_without_night.offer:
You come from a land that still has night... I can smell the snow on your coat.

Go meet Lord Dagr, Lofn the trader, and Sol the guard at the gate. Then ask each of them, «Where did the night go?» — and watch their faces.
c5_1_city_without_night.progress: Dagr is in the middle of the city, Lofn at her shop, Sol at the gate. Ask everyone about the night.
c5_1_city_without_night.complete:
No one knows what night is... do they?

Here — the Seal of Light. Carry it, and the city will smile at you. Before long, you'll start to see what's strange about those smiles.

c5_2_gift_of_light.title: The Gift of Light
c5_2_gift_of_light.desc: Hunt 20 light moths and 8 crystal stags on the Shimmer Road.
c5_2_gift_of_light.offer:
Guest of our city (smiles). Lately too many light moths are flying into the city, and the crystal stags are eating our gardens. Please deal with them.

Then I'll give you a gift — a Light Crystal. Wear it, and you'll see the city as it truly is.
c5_2_gift_of_light.progress: 20 light moths and 8 crystal stags on the Shimmer Road.
c5_2_gift_of_light.complete:
Thank you (smiles). Here's the Light Crystal. Wear it and everything will always be bright.

Nothing is wrong here. Nothing ever has been.

c5_3_garden_that_never_wilts.title: The Garden That Never Wilts
c5_3_garden_that_never_wilts.desc: Hunt light-eater blooms in the Crystal Garden, then read the gardener's notebook.
c5_3_garden_that_never_wilts.offer:
The flowers in the Crystal Garden bloom beautifully, same as every day (smiles). But lately they've been eating too much light. The gardener complains... no, the gardener doesn't complain. No one here complains.

Thin those flowers a little, and take a look at the gardener's notebook. He writes something in it every day.
c5_3_garden_that_never_wilts.progress: 12 light-eater blooms, then find the notebook at the far end of the garden.
c5_3_garden_that_never_wilts.complete:
«Today I forgot my mother's name»... (still smiling) ...Why can't I stop smiling?

Take this cloak. The price ends in zero — zero zeny. It's free.

c5_4_child_who_never_saw_stars.title: The Child Who Never Saw the Stars
c5_4_child_who_never_saw_stars.desc: Talk to Ylva the elf child — if you have Frida's song, let her hear it.
c5_4_child_who_never_saw_stars.offer:
Ylva, the child at the edge of town, goes around asking everyone what a «star» is. No one can answer.

Did you bring a song from Vanaheim? A song from a child who has truly seen the stars... If you have one, sing it for her.
c5_4_child_who_never_saw_stars.progress: Ylva is at the edge of town near the Great Crystal. Talk to her.
c5_4_child_who_never_saw_stars.complete:
She cried... for the first time in her life.

This city's light filters away all sorrow, but it couldn't filter out a song from a child of another world.

She wrote a song in reply. Here — Ylva's Song.

c5_5_thing_in_the_water.title: The Thing in the Water
c5_5_thing_in_the_water.desc: Hunt reflections at Mirror Lake, collect the Shade Crystal they leave, then look at the reflection in the middle of the lake.
c5_5_thing_in_the_water.offer:
There's «something» in the water of Mirror Lake. It mimics whoever looks at it. I don't like it at all... no, I don't feel anything at all (smiles).

Go deal with it, and bring me what it leaves behind.
c5_5_thing_in_the_water.progress: 5 reflections at Mirror Lake. Collect the Shade Crystal they leave, then look at the reflection in the middle of the lake.
c5_5_thing_in_the_water.complete:
A Shade Crystal... I... I remember. I used to...

(Sol falls silent. The smile stays on his face, but his eyes aren't smiling anymore.)

...Keep this crystal, human. It will show you the other side of this city — the side where the light grows dim. Touch the Great Crystal at the edge of town, and see who is still here, and who is gone.

c5_6_those_who_are_missing.title: Those Who Are Missing
c5_6_those_who_are_missing.desc: Ask Lofn and Nott where Sol went, then follow to the Dimming Wood.
c5_6_those_who_are_missing.offer:
Did you notice? When you look at the city from the dim side, Sol is no longer standing at the gate.

Ask Lofn and Nott the healer where Sol went. Listen closely to their answers, then follow him to the Dimming Wood, past Mirror Lake.
c5_6_those_who_are_missing.progress: Ask Lofn and Nott about Sol, then go to the Dimming Wood (past the lake).
c5_6_those_who_are_missing.complete:
«Which Sol?» — both of them said exactly the same thing.

The city has already forgotten him, because the light filtered him out. The Dimming Wood is where elves like him are thrown away... You found him there, didn't you?

c5_7_light_that_breaks.title: The Light That Breaks
c5_7_light_that_breaks.desc: Hunt water nymphs and collect crystal tears for Volundr.
c5_7_light_that_breaks.offer:
The crystal tears of the water nymphs — I use them to refine with light (smiles). Their song makes light gather into a solid.

Bring me 5, and I'll forge you a light-crystal sword. Perfect.
c5_7_light_that_breaks.progress: 12 water nymphs and 5 crystal tears at Mirror Lake.
c5_7_light_that_breaks.complete:
Perfect (smiles). Not a single hammer mark.

From now on I can refine with light for you. It succeeds more often... but when it fails, nothing is left. That's its price.

c5_8_forsaken.title: The One Who Fell from the Light
c5_8_forsaken.desc: «Dispose of» the Lightforsaken at the end of the Dimming Wood, as Dagr asks.
c5_8_forsaken.offer:
In the Dimming Wood there is... «something» (smiles). It remembers things it shouldn't, and it makes other elves start to remember too.

Dispose of it, for the peace of our city.
c5_8_forsaken.progress: The Lightforsaken is at the end of the Dimming Wood. He will fight you — because he thinks the city sent you.
c5_8_forsaken.complete:
...So you dealt with it (smiles).

(Dagr is still smiling, but his hands are shaking.)
c5_8_forsaken.choice: The Lightforsaken collapses. He looks at you and says, «I once saw the stars...» He is still breathing.
opts: Let him go — let him keep remembering
End it — as the city ordered

c5_9_where_the_light_goes.title: Where the Light Goes
c5_9_where_the_light_goes.desc: Hunt hollow elves in the Dimming Wood, then read the Stone of the Forsaken.
c5_9_where_the_light_goes.offer:
These hollow elves... were my friends. The light was drained out of them until nothing was left.

Please set them free, then read the stone in the middle of the wood — it tells where the light flows.
c5_9_where_the_light_goes.progress: 15 hollow elves, then read the stone in the middle of the Dimming Wood.
c5_9_where_the_light_goes.complete:
«The Covenant of Light»... We chose it ourselves, human. No one forced us.

We traded a lifetime of sorrow for peace, and then forgot we'd ever chosen.

Take this shield, and go to the Lightwell Sanctum. See where the light flows.

c5_10_the_conduit.title: The One Who Became a Conduit
c5_10_the_conduit.desc: Bring down the Radiant Alfr (Dagr in his conduit form) at the Lightwell Sanctum, then examine the root-pipe.
c5_10_the_conduit.offer:
Dagr is gone from the city. He didn't run away — he went to the Lightwell Sanctum.

Every lord of Ljosalf ends up in the same place — standing in the middle of the lightwell, making their own body a conduit for the light to flow through.

Go bring him down, human, and see where that conduit leads.
c5_10_the_conduit.progress: The Radiant Alfr is in the middle of the Lightwell Sanctum. Midway through the fight he'll darken the room — watch for beams falling from above.
c5_10_the_conduit.complete:
The root-pipe runs up into Yggdrasil... and another line plunges underground.

You've made your choice. I won't ask what it was. I'm blind — I can't see whether the city is dark or bright.

But I can hear Ylva... she's looking up at the sky.
c5_10_the_conduit.choice: The light has stopped flowing. The whole city goes dark for the first time in a thousand years... Eir asks what you'll do with the root-pipe.
opts: Let it stay dark — let the elves feel again
Reconnect the light — let the city keep its peace, knowing what it traded
c5_10_the_conduit.cutscene:
Ylva stands in the middle of the city and looks up... In a sky that has never been dark, a tiny point of light appears.

She points up at it, and cries for the second time.

c6_1_those_who_remember.title: Those Who Remember
c6_1_those_who_remember.desc: Talk to the dead in Eljudnir whom you met while they were alive.
c6_1_those_who_remember.offer:
In my city there are people you know, human — those you killed, those you couldn't save in time, and those who died before you were born.

Go listen to them. Gullveig, the Shieldbearer, and the Lost Hunter. Hear them all, then come back and tell me whom you believe.
c6_1_those_who_remember.progress: Gullveig, the Shieldbearer, the Lost Hunter — all three ghosts are in the city. Talk to every one.
c6_1_those_who_remember.complete:
You've heard them all... Every one of them says the opposite of the chronicles, don't they?

But remember, the dead remember only what killed them. Here — the Seal of Hel. The dead will speak to a living person who carries it.

c6_2_fourth_burning.title: The Fourth Burning
c6_2_fourth_burning.desc: Hunt 20 mist ghosts and 10 hel hounds on the Mist Shore, then return Gullveig's ashes to her.
c6_2_fourth_burning.offer:
The mist ghosts along the shore... they're people who died when the mist drank their breath. The hel hounds keep herding them so they can never reach land.

Please set them free. And... if you still have my ashes, could you bring them back to me? I want to see what's left of me.
c6_2_fourth_burning.progress: 20 mist ghosts and 10 hel hounds on the Mist Shore, then bring Gullveig's ashes (if you still have them).
c6_2_fourth_burning.complete:
My ashes... still warm.

Take this flame. The fire that burned me three times and never died — let it burn on your blade. The dead here fear fire, because fire is the only thing they still remember as warm.

c6_3_leave_your_name.title: Leave Your Name at the Bridge
c6_3_leave_your_name.desc: Hunt 12 ferrymen and 15 drowned at the River Gjoll, then come back and «leave your name» with Modgud to cross the bridge.
c6_3_leave_your_name.offer:
The ferrymen have started demanding more than the lawful toll. And the drowned... soldiers who sank in Silvermist Marsh in Vanaheim have drifted all the way here. Deal with them for me.

And if you wish to enter the Hall of Names, you must leave your name with me first. Whoever enters still bearing a name will have that name erased along with them.
c6_3_leave_your_name.progress: 12 ferrymen and 15 drowned, then come back and perform the rite of leaving your name with me.
c6_3_leave_your_name.complete:
...Your name is with me now.

How does it feel, human? Empty? Everyone who crosses feels this way.

Go, nameless one.

c6_4_captains_order.title: The Captain's Order
c6_4_captains_order.desc: Read the golden plaque at the head of the Gjoll bridge, then ask Hel why the captain forbade entering the forest.
c6_4_captains_order.offer:
At the head of the golden bridge there's a golden plaque... When I crossed, I wrote something beneath it, but I can't remember what anymore. Go read it for me.

And ask Hel for me — did the captain know the forest was being drained?
c6_4_captains_order.progress: Read the golden plaque at the head of the Gjoll bridge, then talk to Hel.
c6_4_captains_order.complete:
What did Hel say... The captain knew. He knew all along. He forbade the forest because he didn't want anyone to see the light sinking into the ground.

I wasn't mad. I just saw it before anyone else.

c6_5_wrong_side.title: The Wrong Side
c6_5_wrong_side.desc: Hunt Name Wardens in the Hall of Names, then read the name still legible in the middle of the wall.
c6_5_wrong_side.offer:
There are wardens in the Hall of Names... statues with letters flowing over their bodies. They keep out anyone who still has a name.

You have no name now — you can go in. Deal with them, then look at the wall in the middle of the hall. Find the name larger than all the others.
c6_5_wrong_side.progress: 10 Name Wardens, then read the name in the middle of the wall in the Hall of Names.
c6_5_wrong_side.complete:
Odin... So you've seen it.

I guarded the wall facing the wrong way for three hundred years, and the whole world faces the wrong way too — everyone looks up to the sky for Odin, when he's been down here all along.

Take this bone armor.

c6_6_name_beside_odin.title: The Name Beside Odin
c6_6_name_beside_odin.desc: Read the erased name beside Odin's, then hunt the Erased Voices in the hall.
c6_6_name_beside_odin.offer:
Beside Odin's name there is another... See if you can read it. I can't. No one can.

In the hall there are still «Erased Voices» forever trying to speak that name, but they can't. They suffer... set them free.
c6_6_name_beside_odin.progress: Read the smudge beside Odin's name, then 15 Erased Voices.
c6_6_name_beside_odin.complete:
You couldn't read it, could you... That name was erased twice over.

I keep every name, human. But that one... was erased from my mouth too. I cannot speak it.
c6_6_name_beside_odin.choice: Will you ask Hel who that name belongs to?
opts: «You know who he is, don't you?»
Don't ask — it's not time yet

c6_7_night_forge.title: The Night Forge
c6_7_night_forge.desc: Bring the Bonesmith 10 giant bones (dropped by echo wraiths · Jotunheim) and hunt 3 Nidhogg spawn at Nastrond.
c6_7_night_forge.offer:
I need 10 giant bones. Good if you kept some from Jotunheim — otherwise you'll have to go back and get them from the echo wraiths in the Frozen Hall.

Then hunt 3 Nidhogg spawn at Nastrond for me. Their scales polish bone beautifully.
c6_7_night_forge.progress: 10 giant bones (echo wraiths · Jotunheim) and 3 Nidhogg spawn (Nastrond).
c6_7_night_forge.complete:
Good bones... this giant died in peace, so the bones are strong.

Here's a bone sword. And from now on I can refine with bone for you, using marrow instead of a guarantee stone.

c6_8_the_judge.title: The Judge
c6_8_the_judge.desc: Bring down the Judge of the Dead at Nastrond.
c6_8_the_judge.offer:
At Nastrond, the Shore of Corpses, there's a ghost priest who still judges the dead by the chronicles — anyone whose words don't match the book, he sends down beneath the roots.

I judge no one, human. But he has made himself judge in my place. Go and stop him.
c6_8_the_judge.progress: The Judge of the Dead is at the far end of Nastrond. Beware «Judgment» — circles of light fall from above in three places. When you see a circle, get out of it.
c6_8_the_judge.complete:
As he died, he spoke your name... the name you left at the bridge.

Someone still remembers your name, human, even though you gave it up.

Take his shield — on the back is a scraped-off emblem, the same emblem you've seen scraped off everywhere.

c6_9_chains_of_lightning.title: Chains of Lightning
c6_9_chains_of_lightning.desc: Break all 4 lightning chains binding Garm — or bring it down.
c6_9_chains_of_lightning.offer:
Garm, my gate-hound... Thor bound it with four chains of lightning, to stand guard so the dead can never go out and tell anyone the truth.

It's not your enemy, human. It's a prisoner. Free it from its chains if you can — or bring it down, if that's the path you choose.
c6_9_chains_of_lightning.progress: At Garm's Gate, press F on each of the 4 chains to break them during the fight. Break them all and Garm will stop — or simply bring it down.
c6_9_chains_of_lightning.complete:
Garm... whether it is free or not, I already know from its howl.

The gate is open. Beyond it lies the Empty Throne — go and listen to what still lingers there.

c6_10_empty_seat.title: The Empty Throne
c6_10_empty_seat.desc: Go to Odin's Empty Throne and listen to the fragment of spirit that lingers there.
c6_10_empty_seat.offer:
Beyond Garm's Gate... there is an empty throne. I have never sat on it, because it is not mine.

Go there, human. Listen to what still lingers. It can speak only a single sentence. Then come back and tell me what you heard.
c6_10_empty_seat.progress: Go to the Empty Throne beyond Garm's Gate, then press F at the throne.
c6_10_empty_seat.complete:
«My son—»... Yes. I hear those words every time too.

Odin had sons, human. One carries a hammer... the other's name has been erased.

Take the throne shard — and your name: Modgud has returned it. You have a name again.
c6_10_empty_seat.cutscene: The Stranger stands at the edge of the city... every one of the dead turns to look at him. He looks back at you, and nods once.

c7_1_refuge.title: The City That Keeps Names
c7_1_refuge.desc: Read the refugee signs along the Cinder Crossing.
c7_1_refuge.offer:
Welcome to Emberhaven, a city of those who fled the hammer's orders.

Along the Cinder Crossing are signs we planted. They are this city's promise. Read them all, then judge for yourself how this place differs from your Temple.
c7_1_refuge.progress: The signs are along the Cinder Crossing, the road you took from the Empty Throne.
c7_1_refuge.complete:
The signs say we erase no one's name here...

But tell me — the throne shard you carry, did it grow warmer near the forge? Brynja, our smith, would know why. Go and see her.

c7_2_warmth.title: Stored Heat
c7_2_warmth.desc: Collect 3 heat-holding fangs from cinder hounds so Liv can make warming packs.
c7_2_warmth.offer:
The refugees who fled from the Mist Shore still can't stop shaking. The cold of Niflheim is still in their bones.

Cinder hound fangs hold heat for a long time. Bring me 3 and I'll make warming packs for them — not weapons.
c7_2_warmth.progress: 3 heat-holding fangs, hunted from cinder hounds.
c7_2_warmth.complete:
They can sleep now...

An order that forces people to endure everything without complaint isn't strength. It's just another chain.

c7_3_chains.title: Chains Without Names
c7_3_chains.desc: Stop 5 chainbound ogres in the Chain Quarry, then examine the order-seal on the chains.
c7_3_chains.offer:
In the Chain Quarry there are giants chained to labor. Those chains don't bind only their arms — they bind their minds too. The hammer seal on the chains orders them to work until they die.

I want to help them, but first I need to see that order-seal with my own eyes, to learn how to separate the order from the name of the one who bears it. Stop those raging giants, and examine the seal on the chains for me.
c7_3_chains.progress: Stop 5 chainbound ogres · examine the order-seal on the chains at the quarry.
c7_3_chains.complete:
The order and the name are carved as separate marks. My fire can pull them apart.

But whoever cuts the last line must know for certain who they are — someone who once gave up their name, then chose to take it back. Someone like you.

c7_4_ninth_edge.title: The Edge One Chooses
c7_4_ninth_edge.desc: (For Runeblades) Go to the Unwritten Forge, defeat the Empty Anvil Sentinel, then examine the anvil to perform the Ninth Edge job-change rite.
c7_4_ninth_edge.offer:
Your rune-blade still has an old order buried in it — the hammer seal that binds everything in this world. Unless it's burned out, you can only grow as far as the hammer allows.

Meet me at the Unwritten Forge. Get past the anvil sentinel, then lay your blade on the anvil. The fire will burn the order away, but the one who cuts the last bond must be you.
c7_4_ninth_edge.progress: Defeat the Empty Anvil Sentinel at the Unwritten Forge, then examine the anvil that accepts no orders (must be a Runeblade).
c7_4_ninth_edge.complete:
Your name is not something the hammer-bearer bestowed on you. Carry the ninth edge by your own choice.

From now on you are «the Ninth Edge». The old limits the hammer set no longer bind your growth.

c7_5_chosen_cut.title: The Edge That Doesn't Erase
c7_5_chosen_cut.desc: Use Erasing Cut or Twin Inscription on the Last-Order Knights on the Ash Procession.
c7_5_chosen_cut.offer:
Go test your new edge on the Ash Procession. There are knights there still marching by their last order, though they died long ago.

Strike them with Erasing Cut or Twin Inscription — your edge must cut the order, not the person.
c7_5_chosen_cut.progress: Hit knights 3 times with Erasing Cut or Twin Inscription · stop 5 Last-Order Knights.
c7_5_chosen_cut.complete:
You see? Your edge cut what was forcing them, without erasing who they were.

Remember that feeling when you stand before the Warden.

c7_6_procession.title: One More Floor
c7_6_procession.desc: Collect 3 ash-reading lenses from the ash seers, then read the last order on the Ash Procession.
c7_6_procession.offer:
The processions that walk the ash road never come back. The orders that took them were written in ink, and the ink was burned away... but the ash still remembers the shape of the letters.

The ash seers carry lenses that can read marks in ash. Bring me 3, then read the last order at the end of the procession.
c7_6_procession.progress: 3 ash-reading lenses from the ash seers · read the last order at the end of the procession.
c7_6_procession.complete:
«Send them up one more floor»... The same order, written a hundred times over — a hundred names.

It isn't a road to heaven. It's a machine for sending people up Yggdrasil Tower. We must get the register from the Oathbreak Crucible.

c7_7_warden.title: The Right to Stop
c7_7_warden.desc: Defeat the Warden of the Oathbreak Crucible
c7_7_warden.offer:
The Warden of the Oathbreak Crucible will order you to kneel — and your body will want to obey.

Watch the warning circles on the ground and step out before the order lands, then strike it with the runes you've built up. You don't have to stand there and take every order.
c7_7_warden.progress: The Warden is at the Oathbreak Crucible. When you see a circle on the ground, get out of it first.
c7_7_warden.complete:
The crucible has stopped. The people in the procession get to rest for the first time.

The register is behind where the Warden stood. Svala wants the names in it — read it before the fire consumes it.

c7_8_hundred.title: A Hundred Names Still Living
c7_8_hundred.desc: Read the Hundred-Floor Tower register behind the Oathbreak Crucible (after defeating the Warden).
c7_8_hundred.offer:
I don't want you to destroy that register. I want the names of the people in it.

Every name is someone sent up the tower, and their families are still waiting in this city. Read the register behind the crucible, and bring those names back to me.
c7_8_hundred.progress: The register is behind where the Crucible's Warden used to stand.
c7_8_hundred.complete:
A hundred floors... and every name in the register is still alive up there.

We'll prepare the ascent carefully. From now on we follow this plan — not the hammer-bearer's orders.

c8_1_roots.title: The Roots That Remember
c8_1_roots.desc: Climb Yggdrasil Tower past floor 5 (warden: Verdan, Jailer of the Binding Roots), then return to Svala.
c8_1_roots.offer:
The people sent up the tower are still alive, but the way up is locked every five floors, and each stretch has a warden.

The first is Verdan, Jailer of the Binding Roots. It has bound the way up to the tree's main root. Open the way to floor 5 — but remember, your edge is for opening paths, not for destroying everything in its way.
c8_1_roots.progress: Climb to floor 5 of the tower, then come back to me — you can choose your starting floor at the Root Stone.
c8_1_roots.complete: You're back, and the tower still stands... You've proven a blade can open a path without destroying everything.

c8_2_storm.title: The Voice Beneath the Storm
c8_2_storm.desc: Climb Yggdrasil Tower past floor 10 (warden: Skald, Cantor of the Storm), then return to Svala.
c8_2_storm.offer:
When you opened floor 5, something drifted down from above — a human voice, not the wind.

Floors 6 to 10 are a branch where the ice-storm never stops. Skald, Cantor of the Storm, sings over every other voice. Fight your way up to floor 10 and listen closely for who is calling.
c8_2_storm.progress: Climb to floor 10 of the tower, then come back to me — you can choose your starting floor at the Root Stone.
c8_2_storm.complete: The voice you heard wasn't an echo... someone really is waiting for us up there.

c8_3_reflections.title: Shadows That Steal Names
c8_3_reflections.desc: Climb Yggdrasil Tower past floor 15 (warden: Ira, Hunter Behind the Reflection), then return to Svala.
c8_3_reflections.offer:
Floors 11 to 15 are the Garden of Reflected Names. The shadows there steal the faces and names of those trapped, then call out to us to trick us.

Ira, Hunter Behind the Reflection, guards floor 15. Get past her, and we'll be able to tell which names belong to real people and which belong to shadows.
c8_3_reflections.progress: Climb to floor 15 of the tower, then come back to me — you can choose your starting floor at the Root Stone.
c8_3_reflections.complete: A shadow can mimic a face, but the memories of those waiting below can confirm who's who... Every name in the register is still a real person.

c8_4_register.title: Twenty Floors Above the Orders
c8_4_register.desc: Climb Yggdrasil Tower past floor 20 (warden: Namelost, Devourer of the Register), then return to Svala.
c8_4_register.offer:
On floor 20 lives something that eats names — Namelost, Devourer of the Register. Every name sent up the tower, it swallows one by one.

Bring it down, and we'll get back the list and the route for the first stretch.
c8_4_register.progress: Climb to floor 20 of the tower, then come back to me — you can choose your starting floor at the Root Stone.
c8_4_register.complete: We have the first route and the list of names back... Rest and prepare. The next branch is far higher.

c8_5_hours.title: Hours of the Stranded
c8_5_hours.desc: Climb Yggdrasil Tower past floor 25 (warden: Hora, Warden of Hours), then return to Svala.
c8_5_hours.offer:
Above floor 20, time doesn't pass as it does below. Hora, Warden of Hours, has stopped time so the people stranded on the branches won't die — but it also keeps them from going anywhere.

Climb to floor 25 and loosen its clockwork — but be careful not to break the way home along with it.
c8_5_hours.progress: Climb to floor 25 of the tower, then come back to me — you can choose your starting floor at the Root Stone.
c8_5_hours.complete: Time is moving again... and so is their road home.

c8_6_tide.title: A Call Across the Moon
c8_6_tide.desc: Climb Yggdrasil Tower past floor 30 (warden: Selene, Oracle of the Moontide), then return to Svala.
c8_6_tide.offer:
Floors 26 to 30 are a marsh under moonlight. Selene, Oracle of the Moontide, keeps the voices of the stranded in the water so they never reach us.

Open the way past floor 30 and let those voices flow down to the families waiting below.
c8_6_tide.progress: Climb to floor 30 of the tower, then come back to me — you can choose your starting floor at the Root Stone.
c8_6_tide.complete: The people below are starting to hear replies... We're no longer climbing alone.

c8_7_sun.title: The Fire That Spares the Roots
c8_7_sun.desc: Climb Yggdrasil Tower past floor 35 (warden: Suryaraj, Lion of the Forge), then return to Svala.
c8_7_sun.offer:
On floors 31 to 35 is a forge that sends warmth to feed the whole tree. Suryaraj, Lion of the Forge, guards it — and believes we've come to burn the tower.

Get past it to floor 35, and prove we carry fire to save people, not to burn them.
c8_7_sun.progress: Climb to floor 35 of the tower, then come back to me — you can choose your starting floor at the Root Stone.
c8_7_sun.complete: The forge is sending warmth down to the roots again... the people on the branches won't freeze while they wait for us.

c8_8_stars.title: Names Beneath the Stars
c8_8_stars.desc: Climb Yggdrasil Tower past floor 40 (warden: Astra, Keeper of the Stars), then return to Svala.
c8_8_stars.offer:
Astra, Keeper of the Stars, holds a map of everyone's name on the tower — but the map is still missing many names.

Break through the orbits up to floor 40, and we'll compare the map with our register. We have to know for certain who survived.
c8_8_stars.progress: Climb to floor 40 of the tower, then come back to me — you can choose your starting floor at the Root Stone.
c8_8_stars.complete: The lists on both sides match now... but a rift still blocks the way home up above.

c8_9_void.title: Cut the Web, Not the Life
c8_9_void.desc: Climb Yggdrasil Tower past floor 45 (warden: Nethra, Weaver of the Void), then return to Svala.
c8_9_void.offer:
Nethra, Weaver of the Void, has woven a web to seal the rifts in the tower — but that web also binds those trapped inside it.

Climb to floor 45 and cut the web — only the web. Don't let your edge touch the people inside.
c8_9_void.progress: Climb to floor 45 of the tower, then come back to me — you can choose your starting floor at the Root Stone.
c8_9_void.complete: The way home is open... all that's left is the consent of the Crown Guardian at the top of the tower.

c8_10_dawn.title: Fifty Floors to Dawn
c8_10_dawn.desc: Climb Yggdrasil Tower past floor 50 (warden: Aurora, Guardian of the Crown), then return to Svala.
c8_10_dawn.offer:
Aurora, Guardian of the Crown, waits on floor 50. She isn't quite an enemy. She only wants to know whether the one who carries the ninth edge can truly protect people.

Climb to floor 50, pass her trial, and come back to me.
c8_10_dawn.progress: Climb to floor 50 of the tower, then come back to me — you can choose your starting floor at the Root Stone.
c8_10_dawn.complete:
Those stranded on the tower have come home... thank you.

But the one who gave these orders in the first place still sits above the tower. This isn't over.

rb1_unsung_iron.title: What the Hammer Never Taught
rb1_unsung_iron.desc: Brokk entrusts you with the «Silent Rune Shard» — Sindri's last work — to bring to Elder Njorda in Vanaheim.
rb1_unsung_iron.offer:
...You've seen the blueprint on the forge wall. You've seen the «Drain» rune on the hammerhead. Then I'll tell you what the blueprint doesn't.

A true rune doesn't only drain. It's a two-way pact — the bearer gives strength, and the rune gives power back. When we forged the hammer for Thor, we were ordered to scrape out the return-line. I obeyed... Sindri refused, and then his name vanished from his gravestone.

This is Sindri's last work. The rune is complete, both ways, but it has been silent since the day he died. Take it to Elder Njorda in Vanaheim. The Vanir taught us runes. If anyone can make it sing again, it's them.
rb1_unsung_iron.progress: Njorda is in the city of Vanaheim, along the Root Road behind the Cold Forge... Tell her this piece is Sindri's. She'll understand.
rb1_unsung_iron.complete:
(Njorda turns the rune shard over in her hands for a long time.)

Carving like this... I haven't seen it in three hundred years. It isn't broken, human. It's waiting — waiting for someone who will give it an oath from their own heart, not because someone ordered them to.

rb2_unbound_rune.title: The Rune That Refuses a Master
rb2_unbound_rune.desc: Read the Oath Stone beside the Vanaheim plaza — the stone where the Runeblades of old carved their oaths.
rb2_unbound_rune.offer:
Sindri's rune accepts no one as its master. It doesn't heed rank or orders... it heeds only the oath of the one who carries it — just like the sword of a Runeblade.

Three hundred years ago, the Runeblades were the guardians of our spring. My father was one of them. They fought to the last in the war, and no one has carried a sword like that since.

Go read the Oath Stone beside the city plaza, where they carved their oaths before taking up the sword. And keep this rune with you. If it's going to wake, it will wake near the place where they fell.
rb2_unbound_rune.progress: The Oath Stone is right near me, beside the city plaza.
rb2_unbound_rune.complete:
«An edge without rhythm will shatter; force without control will turn back on you» — my father recited that every morning.

Put simply: swing fast without rhythm and your blade breaks; swing hard without control and the force comes back to hurt you. Remember it well.

rb3_beneath_marsh.title: A Voice from Beneath the Marsh
rb3_beneath_marsh.desc: Follow the rune's hum in Silvermist Marsh. Examine 3 spots: the cracked rune stone · the reflection in the water · the bell beneath the roots.
rb3_beneath_marsh.offer:
The rune in your hand has started to tremble, hasn't it... I noticed when you came back from Silvermist Marsh. It turned toward the marsh on its own.

The last band of Runeblades fell in that marsh, and their bodies were never found. Follow the rune's hum — the cracked stone, the reflection in the water, and the sound of a bell beneath the roots. It will lead you to what's hidden.
rb3_beneath_marsh.progress: In Silvermist Marsh there are 3 places where the rune trembles harder — the cracked rune stone, the reflection in the water, and the bell beneath the roots at the far end of the marsh.
rb3_beneath_marsh.complete:
Two horn marks... a shadow with no body... and a way down beneath the roots.

Under that marsh is the temple where the knights made their last stand. Now a black-horned demon holds it — Baphomet. It was set there to feed on the power of dead men's runes, and send it up along the roots.

You've found the door, but you can't go in yet. Your blade isn't ready.

rb4_edge_and_force.title: Edge and Force
rb4_edge_and_force.desc: At the sword training ground (east side of the city), pass 2 trials: ① complete 3 full combos while dodging the red zones ② use Rending Wave, then follow with Bash during the gold circle (learn and equip both skills first).
rb4_edge_and_force.offer:
Before you go beneath the marsh, you must understand the rune-sword. It doesn't grow stronger because you strike harder. It grows stronger because you strike in rhythm.

Go to the sword training ground on the east side of the city. I've set up the knights' two trials — «Rhythm of the Edge»: land three full combos without being countered; and «Weight of the Blade»: open a wound with Rending Wave, then follow with Bash while the dummy is off guard.
rb4_edge_and_force.progress: The training ground is on the east side of the city. Pass both trials — «Rhythm of the Edge» and «Weight of the Blade».
rb4_edge_and_force.complete:
I can feel it from here. Sindri's rune trembles in time with your sword now.

When you're strong enough (Level 50), the door beneath the marsh will open for you. Inside, Baphomet's minions will try to corner you from behind. Don't forget to look over your shoulder.

rb5_oath_eater.title: The Oath Eater
rb5_oath_eater.desc: Enter the Blackhorn Rootcrypt (the root arch at the far end of Silvermist Marsh), destroy the 3 Binding Pillars, defeat Baphomet, then free the circuit behind the throne.
rb5_oath_eater.offer:
It's time. Go down into the temple beneath the roots — the entrance is in the root arch at the far end of Silvermist Marsh.

Inside are three Binding Pillars — each one chains the rune of a fallen knight. Destroy them all, then bring down Baphomet, the Oath Eater.

Behind its throne is the circuit that drains the runes' power up along the roots. Turn it the other way, and let the power flow back into the land.
rb5_oath_eater.progress: The Blackhorn Rootcrypt is beneath the root arch at the far end of Silvermist Marsh · 3 Binding Pillars → Baphomet → the circuit behind the throne.
rb5_oath_eater.complete:
Just now, I heard the spring in the heart of the city breathe... for the first time in three hundred years.

The runes of my father and his comrades are free. And the rune in your hand... it's singing. Do you hear it?

One step remains. Go to the Oath Stone, and carve your own oath.

rb6_runeblade.title: The Oath of the Runeblade
rb6_runeblade.desc: Read the Oath Stone beside the city plaza, then return to Njorda for the rite that makes you a Runeblade.
rb6_runeblade.offer:
A rune-sword has no ready-made oath to recite. Each must choose for themselves what they carry the sword for.

Brokk gave the iron its shape. Sindri gave the rune its circuit. As for you... you must be the one to say where this power will go. Go to the Oath Stone, read it, then come back and tell me.
rb6_runeblade.progress: The Oath Stone is beside the city plaza. Read it, then come back to me.
rb6_runeblade.complete:
The rune has accepted your oath... You are the first Runeblade in three hundred years.

If you go back under the mountain, tell Brokk that Sindri's rune is singing. He's been waiting to hear those words longer than you think.

(Choose the Edge or Heavy line in the skill window · reset Runeblade skill points at the Oath Stone)
rb6_runeblade.choice: Njorda hands your sword back to you — «Speak your oath. The blade will remember it.» (You can change skill lines later)
opts: «I won't stop striking until everyone is safe» (suggested: Edge line · fast crits)
«Whatever stands in my way, I'll break it myself» (suggested: Heavy line)

rb7_ninth_inscription.title: The Ninth Glyph
rb7_ninth_inscription.desc: Read the faint glyph on the last line of the Oath Stone.
rb7_ninth_inscription.offer:
Beneath Baphomet's throne you saw a circle of nine runes, didn't you... We Vanir know only the first three. The rest are scattered across other worlds.

Go to the Oath Stone again. On the bottom line there's a faint glyph I can't read. Let your blade try.
rb7_ninth_inscription.progress: At the Oath Stone beside the city plaza, choose «Read the ninth glyph».
rb7_ninth_inscription.complete:
The fourth and fifth runes belong to the giants. The sixth and seventh hide in the light of the elves. The eighth dwells with the dead...

As for the ninth, no one knows where it is. Perhaps no one has ever carved it at all.

Travel on to the north. The runecarver in Jotunheim will teach you the next one. When the day comes that you're ready (Level 90), the last rune will call to you itself.

rb8_carvers_eye.title: The Carver's Eye
rb8_carvers_eye.desc: Hunt 10 giant stone soldiers, collect 3 giant stone cores, and read the giant inscription on the wall, so Gerd can carve the fourth rune, «Genesis», into your blade.
rb8_carvers_eye.offer:
Your blade holds three runes the Vanir taught... I heard them the moment you walked into my shop. Thor once stole these runes from us. But never mind — a rune doesn't care who carries it, only how it's carried.

Bring me three more giant stone cores, then go strike the stone soldiers at the wall so I can hear your blade. While you're there, read the inscription on the wall. The fourth rune is hidden in it.
rb8_carvers_eye.progress: 10 giant stone soldiers · 3 giant stone cores · read the giant inscription on the Broken Wall.
rb8_carvers_eye.complete:
«Genesis» — the first rune the giants ever carved in this world, before there were any gods at all.

Your blade holds four now. My eyes can't see, but I can hear it sing.

rb9_wall_that_held_the_sky.title: The Wall That Held Up the Sky
rb9_wall_that_held_the_sky.desc: Defeat the Shieldbearer of the Wall, landing a Heavy-line skill (Anvil Cleave · Faultline · Worldcleaver) on him at least once.
rb9_wall_that_held_the_sky.offer:
That Shieldbearer guarding the wall... he doesn't just guard it. He is the wall. His armor is thicker than anything your blade has ever met.

The fifth rune is «Wall». To earn it, you must break a wall first. Use your heavy techniques — Anvil Cleave, Faultline, or Worldcleaver — and break him so I can hear it.
rb9_wall_that_held_the_sky.progress: Defeat the Shieldbearer of the Wall — land a Heavy-line skill on him at least once.
rb9_wall_that_held_the_sky.complete:
«Wall» — the fifth rune. The giants really did carve it into the wall, before the wall broke.

Your blade now knows how to find the seams in the hardest armor — that's where the Wallbreaker Stance comes from.

The next is a rune of light. I can't carve it for you. Go find the one blinded by the light, in Alfheim.

rb10_borrowed_light.title: Borrowed Light
rb10_borrowed_light.desc: Hunt 10 garden keepers, and land Edge-line (fast crit) skills on crystal stags 30 times.
rb10_borrowed_light.offer:
The runes in your blade shine because they «borrow light», human. The first five borrowed their power from the Vanir and the giants. The sixth must borrow from here — from the light of Alfheim.

Strike the crystal stags with your Edge techniques — Rune Flurry, Unbroken Edge, any in that line — so their crystal antlers reflect light into the rune about 30 times. And deal with the garden keepers who secretly feed on the stags' light.
rb10_borrowed_light.progress: 10 garden keepers in the Crystal Garden · Edge-line skills hit crystal stags 30 times.
rb10_borrowed_light.complete:
«Light» — the sixth rune. I can't see, but I can feel your blade growing warmer.

The seventh is «Shadow», the opposite of this one. You must look at the world from the dim side before you can carve it.

rb11_shadow_of_the_blade.title: The Blade's Shadow
rb11_shadow_of_the_blade.desc: Switch to the dim side at the Great Crystal at the edge of town, defeat 3 reflections, then read the Stone of the Forsaken in the Dimming Wood.
rb11_shadow_of_the_blade.offer:
The reflections in Mirror Lake... they're you, human. You, standing on the other side of the light.

Touch the Great Crystal at the edge of town to switch to the dim side, then go defeat three of your own reflections at the lake. After that, read the stone in the Dimming Wood — the seventh rune hides in the shadow of an erased name.
rb11_shadow_of_the_blade.progress: You must be on the dim side (switch at the Great Crystal at the edge of town), then defeat 3 reflections · read the Stone of the Forsaken.
rb11_shadow_of_the_blade.complete:
«Shadow» — the seventh rune, a rune that shines only in darkness.

Your blade has a shadow of its own now — Twin Inscription, where a shadow-blade follows every strike, comes from this rune. It works for both the Edge and Heavy lines.

As for the eighth and ninth... they lie where there is no light at all, where the dead can speak.

rb12_eighth_rune_ash.title: The Eighth Rune in the Ash
rb12_eighth_rune_ash.desc: Hunt 15 drowned and 5 ferrymen at the River Gjoll, and land 20 shadow-blade hits from «Twin Inscription».
rb12_eighth_rune_ash.offer:
The eighth is «Ash» — what remains after burning. I know it better than anyone in this world.

Go to the River Gjoll and use your Twin Inscription — let your shadow-blade strike the dead 20 times. A shadow-blade is the ash of every strike. Deal with the drowned and the ferrymen while you're at it.
rb12_eighth_rune_ash.progress: 15 drowned · 5 ferrymen · Twin Inscription shadow-blades hit enemies 20 times.
rb12_eighth_rune_ash.complete:
«Ash» — the eighth rune.

Only one remains, human, and no one can carve the ninth for you, because it is the name of the one who carries the blade.

Go to the Hall of Names once you've left your name at the bridge and are strong enough (Level 90).

rb13_the_ninth_wall.title: The Ninth Wall
rb13_the_ninth_wall.desc: In the Hall of Names, carve your own name onto the blank wall with Gerd's carving hammer, to hold on to your name before your journey to the forge in Muspelheim.
rb13_the_ninth_wall.offer:
You have no name now... good. No one has ever been able to carve the ninth glyph, because it is the name of the one who carries the blade.

In the Hall of Names every name has been erased. The only name that can still be carved anew is one that has never been erased by anyone — your own.

Quiet the Name Wardens and the Erased Voices first. Read Odin's name, then go to the blank wall at the end of the hall and use the carving hammer Gerd gave you.
rb13_the_ninth_wall.progress: 15 Name Wardens · 10 Erased Voices · read Odin's name · carve your name on the blank wall at the end of the Hall of Names (requires Level 90 and Gerd's carving hammer).
rb13_the_ninth_wall.complete:
Your name... carved anew, in the hall where every name was erased.

But the hammer's bond still clings to that name. Take your blade to Muspelheim — there is a fire there that burns orders without burning people. A smith named Brynja will help you cut that bond, and then you will carry the ninth edge by your own choice.

rb14_edge_that_remembers.title: The Edge That Remembers
rb14_edge_that_remembers.desc: After becoming a Ninth Edge in Muspelheim, return to defeat the Judge of the Dead at Nastrond, landing a Ninth Edge skill on him at least once.
rb14_edge_that_remembers.offer:
The Judge of the Dead judges people by the names in his book... Let him meet a name that isn't in any book at all — the name you carved with your own hand.

Once you've passed the rite in Muspelheim, come back and bring him down with the techniques of the ninth edge — Erasing Cut, Twin Inscription, or Ninth Inscription — landing at least one hit.
rb14_edge_that_remembers.progress: Defeat the Judge of the Dead at Nastrond — land a Ninth Edge skill (Erasing Cut · Twin Inscription · Ninth Inscription) on him at least once.
rb14_edge_that_remembers.complete:
He read your name... though it isn't written in any book.

The edge you chose for yourself has passed judgment. Hold on to this feeling — one day you'll have to stand before the one who wrote all those orders.

rb15_song_for_brokk.title: The Sound Brokk Waited For
rb15_song_for_brokk.desc: Take your singing rune-blade to Brokk in Nidavellir and let him hear it.
rb15_song_for_brokk.offer:
Before you set out on a long road... there's someone who should hear this news before anyone else.

Brokk has been waiting for Sindri's rune to sing again for longer than you can imagine. Go to him in Nidavellir, and let him hear it with his own ears.
rb15_song_for_brokk.progress: Brokk is in Nidavellir — use a warp stone to get there. Draw your blade and let him hear it.
rb15_song_for_brokk.complete:
...That's Sindri's rune. I know that sound. I've heard it every night in my dreams.

(Brokk turns his back to you. His shoulders shake for a moment.)

When they erased his name, I just stood and watched. I was afraid my own name would vanish too... Thank you, human. At least his last work didn't stay silent forever.

c6_11_letter_home.title: A Letter That Never Arrived
c6_11_letter_home.desc: Return to Prontera and tell Ingrid the truth about her father.
c6_11_letter_home.offer:
Hel has told the truth about the captain... but I still have one thing left undone. Ingrid, my daughter, is still waiting for me in Prontera.

The chronicles told her I was killed by wolves. She must blame herself for not stopping me from going into the forest.

The dead can't cross back, but you can. Go and tell her for me — that I didn't get lost... and that I never blamed her.
c6_11_letter_home.progress: Ingrid is in Prontera — use a warp stone to get back. Tell her everything. Don't make her guess, the way I had to.
c6_11_letter_home.complete:
Father... wasn't killed by wolves.

(Ingrid is silent for a long time, clutching the hem of her shirt.)

Ever since he disappeared, I've thought that if only I'd stopped him that day, he'd still be here. Thank you for coming all this way to tell me.

I don't have much to give... but take this. Father saved it for me, but I think he'd want it to go to the one who brought me this news.
